problem: Standard VLN benchmarks and agents assume every instruction is feasible and the target exists, so agents cannot explicitly report failure. When the target is absent they hallucinate similar objects, search indefinitely, or stop prematurely. Imitation-learned agents in particular lack a 'search finished' signal.
motivation: Humans often mislocate objects when instructing robots, giving well-formed but factually false instructions. Absence cannot be confirmed from one viewpoint, so the agent must gather evidence through exploration under partial observability before answering NOT-FOUND. Supervised agents navigate between rooms well but under-explore inside the room, while LLM agents have commonsense for search but navigate poorly at floorplan level.
key_idea: Build VLN-NF, a false-premise VLN benchmark (LLM rewrites the target, VLM verifies absence) with the REV-SPL metric, and solve it with ROAM: a room-level supervised navigator followed by an LLM/VLM in-room explorer guided by a free-space clearance prior (FREE).
insight: Splitting the task by strength works: the ablation shows an LLM-only controller reaches the target room only 7.8% of the time (REV-SPL 0.8), and adding a room-label-trained navigator raises Reach SR to 59.4% (REV-SPL 5.6). FREE geometric clearance cues add coverage (79.2 to 82.1%) and REV-SPL (5.6 to 6.1) without changing reaching. REV-SPL also exposes an efficiency-thoroughness trade-off: GPT-4o decides better than GPT-3.5 but explores far longer (22.0 vs 9.9), so its REV-SPL is lower.
method: Dataset construction (rewrite-and-verify): gpt-3.5-turbo replaces the REVERIE target object with a plausible object absent from the target room's object list (avoid list); GLIP (threshold 0.7) runs over all room panoramas, and any detected object is blacklisted and resampled. A 5% audit found <2% errors. Each REVERIE instance is paired one-to-one with an NF counterpart.

Reference exploration protocol: reach path is the GT path prefix up to room entry. For landmark-cued instructions, the reference is a brute-force TSP over viewpoints that see the original target. Otherwise it is a greedy new-object-coverage explorer, and pairs below 85% coverage are discarded.
REV-SPL metric: per-episode product of room reached, correct decision, object coverage C_i and an exploration-length efficiency term, alongside Reach SR, Reach&Decision SR, Reach SPL and Coverage.

Room-Level Navigator: DUET fine-tuned on VLN-NF using only reach-to-room paths (room labels), with the best model chosen by Reach SR. It runs until the agent enters the target room or a step budget ends, then hands off to the explorer.

In-room Explorer: NavGPT-style LLM (GPT-3.5 or GPT-4o) using VLM captions and Grounding-DINO detections (threshold 0.75). It outputs FOUND on detection, otherwise keeps exploring and outputs NOT-FOUND when the room is exhausted or the budget is reached.

FREE (Free-space Raycasting Estimation Engine): Grounded-SAM segments floor and door frames, the mask is back-projected to 3D, and 10 cm raycasts toward each candidate viewpoint give a clearance distance that is added to the LLM prompt to favor larger unsearched regions.

setting.backbone: DUET room navigator (fine-tuned) + GPT-3.5-turbo / GPT-4o (frozen) explorer with Grounding-DINO, Grounded-SAM and captioning VLM
setting.model_size: DUET-scale (not stated exactly); LLMs are API models
setting.training_data: DUET fine-tuned on VLN-NF train reach paths (2,362 pairs / 4,724 instructions, room-level supervision only); the LLM explorer is training-free
setting.observation: Matterport3D panoramic RGB (discretized views) with depth/camera parameters for FREE raycasting
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints plus STOP/FOUND and NOT-FOUND
setting.privileged: Room labels and object annotations are used for training, evaluation and reference paths. At test time no GT room entry or oracle hand-off is used, but the target room is parsed from the instruction by Gemini 1.5 Flash (Room-Object Extractor).

results: On VLN-NF val-unseen, ROAM-GPT-3.5 reaches 6.1 REV-SPL, 45% above the supervised DUET (4.2) and above MapGPT (3.2), SoM-Gemini (1.5) and NavGPT (1.0). ROAM-GPT-4o has the best Reach SR (62.6%) and Reach&Decision SR (41.4%) but a lower REV-SPL (5.6) because it explores longer. On feasible REVERIE val-unseen, FREE raises SR from 42.0 to 45.2 and SPL from 23.7 to 25.1.
limitations: Strict filtering keeps only about 45% of REVERIE episodes, and only one false-premise type is covered (target absent from the specified room). Absolute REV-SPL values are low (about 6%), and the metric is complex.
Performance depends on a fixed Grounding-DINO confidence threshold, which may not transfer to new domains. Path quality was not formally assessed, and no recovery policy exists after NOT-FOUND.
Only Matterport3D/REVERIE is used, with no real-robot tests. Baselines are adapted rather than designed for the task.
